benedict-1399-1403.summary: Benedict XIII (Pedro de Luna), besieged in Avignon, writes in cipher to his agent Francesc Climent (Çapera) in Barcelona on the Schism diplomacy of 1399-1403: the embassy of Aragon, Castile and Navarre, the 'submission' he refused, the see of Lérida, a demand for 3,000 francs, and the bulls for Castile's restitution of obedience.
benedict-1399-1403.en:
R1. ... [of the King of Aragon] with the Duke of Burgundy.

R2. And therefore the business is to be held thus in suspense, [?neither] [?approving] [?nor] [?disapproving]. [?Of]
[?the] [?Cardinal] [?of] [?Catania],

R3. that he is going back to Sicily; but others assert that [the King of Aragon], having been made chancellor, is to
remain in Catalonia.

R4. And above all write how he behaves in our affairs. On the matter of the goods of Pere de Bosc: we therefore wrote to
[the King of Aragon] that you would tell him our mind, so that no one else should claim this for himself, and that [the
King of Aragon] should rather thank him than us. So you will tell him that it pleases us and we are content that he
receive [them] at his will;

snip.cap: Benedict XIII to Climent, 22 June 1400, last page: clear Latin with runs of cipher signs; line 1 ends with the name sign for the King of Aragon and cum duce Burgundie in cipher
snip.credit: S. Puig y Puig, Pedro de Luna (1920), p. 475, facsimile of Arxiu Capitular de Barcelona, Documentos inéditos del obispo Çapera no. 1068; via Google Books

system: Simple substitution, one invented or letter-shaped sign per letter (20 values: a hook, b T-bar, c and i a single o, o a double loop, d double cross, e delta, f flagged sigma, g 4-shape, h 2-shape, l looped d, m footed epsilon, n n, p inverted T, q…
